meaning:
Juice WRLD refers to the number “Triple 9” or “999” in both his music and socials. On June 15, 2017, Juice released his third mixtape tilted, JuiceWRLD 9 9 9, which is also his Instagram handle.

In modern culture, the number “666” has become a widely recognized symbol for the devil or evil. Juice, knowing this, decided to flip the number to signify fighting off bad energy or being opposite to the devil.

He went in detail when he tweeted about the meaning in February of 2018:

I took the hell I was going through (666) and flipped it over into something positive (999)

Even after his tragic passing, his message stays strong and has touched many artists such as Halsey, a New Jersey singer, who Juice collaborated with, got “999” tattooed to honor Juice.

Em also paid tribute to Rakim, who is widely regarded as one of the most skilled and influential MCs of all time, on his October 2013 track, “Rap God.”  Rakim pioneered the use of sophisticated rhyme patterns in his flow, employing devices like internal and multisyllabic rhymes that Eminem has also mastered.

While at one time he was forced to move into his mother’s mobile home with his child’s mom Kim and their daughter Hailie, Eminem could now fill a park full of trailers with money, as Forbes reports he is worth well over $200 million, earning $50 million in 2019 alone.

“On the toilet bowl” demonstrates the level of respect Em has for his rivals, whom he feels he is ready to “shit on” even at his most vulnerable and unprepared.

Incidentally, Em was listening to “Paid In Full” when he went live on IG to show off his prodigious Ms. Pac Man skills shortly before flushing one such challenger, Machine Gun Kelly, with the release of Killshot.

Attila the Hun was the leader of the nomadic tribe of the Huns from 434 to 453. During his reign, he was an awe-inspiring warrior and emperor and was called the “scourge of God” by his enemies.

Eminem previously mentioned Attila the Hun on his May 2002 track “Say What You Say” and on Royce Da 5'9"’s May 2018 track “Caterpillar”:

There is a long, racist history of using gorilla imagery to represent Black men as powerful, feral creatures to terrify white people; Eminem describing himself as a “vanilla gorilla” is a boast about being big, powerful and white, but with an allusion to the way his use of cultural Blackness once shocked and terrified white America. “Vanilla” to represent a white rapper might also allude to the infamously wack white rapper Vanilla Ice, whose plummet in cultural popularity created a glass ceiling for white rappers that Eminem was forced to break.

However, the rumors resurfaced in 2017 after he released his ninth studio album, Revival, which received poor reviews from fans and critics alike, and incited people to believe he would retire. Nevertheless, even though Revival did not do well with critics, it still peaked at number one on Billboard 200 and in several other countries overseas.

Following the backlash of Revival, in August 2018 Em' released Kamikaze, and addressed the poor reviews and negative comments that Revival received. It might also be worth noting that in 2010, Eminem hinted that he might retire at the age of 50, during an interview with MTV:

Honestly, I don’t know how much longer I have in this game […] I do love it so much. But even if I was rapping at 50, I don’t know if I would put it out. I know it always makes me feel better to lay things to tape, and — ‘lay the tape.’ See, I’m old school.

meaning:
This is a play on words with the Apache line.

The Apache are a group of culturally related Native American tribes, and Native American tribes have recognized history/association with running casinos and gambling.

Therefore, this “stack chips” line is a reference to that. Native Americans literally stack (gaming) chips in casinos. More than that, stack chips is an idiom meaning to win, but Em compares himself not to the player in the casino but to those who run the casino itself. Em, like the house, always wins.

In poker, “chips” are often used to represent currency, when not gambling with real money. Em brags of his own wealth, while comparing others to potato chips.

Cheeto’s are a brand of snack made by Frito-Lay, which ironically aren’t even made of potato, though they are categorized with other potato chip snacks.



Additionally, cheese is slang for money, as Cheetos contains cheese flavor but no actual cheese.

The term became more popular after Nas‘ December 2001 diss track “Ether,” where he responded to Hov’s claim from September 2001’s “Takeover” that Nas’ bodyguards outperformed him on the November 2000 track, “Oochie Wally,” famously applauding Em for outdoing JAY on “Renegade”:

line: In her eyes, I’m still her hero (Yeah) Bank account got commas and zeros (Yeah)
vault_lines: In her eyes, I'm still her hero (Yeah)
Bank account got commas and zeros (Yeah)
meaning:
This line is a fun play on words and portrays Juices’ love for comic books. The line begins with Juice enunciating “her eyes, I’m” similar to how one would pronounce “horizon.” This is because right after, he follows with “I’m still her hero.” Horizon is a little known black DC superhero introduced in “The Movement #9 (2014).”

This little piece of wordplay is followed by the line “bank account got commas and zeros”, which of course is just him saying he has a large amount of money in his bank account, but the way he delivers this line ties into the horizon word play from earlier. Commas look like small 9’s, which when you add the zero added later in the line makes 90. Horizon is brought back to the discussion but this time, more in the sense of the actual scientific horizon instead of the DC superhero. The Horizon is the boundary where the sky meets the ground or sea. It can always be seen at a 90 degree angle from the observers zenith which tied back into the commas and zeros juice was discussing earlier. The way Juice chooses to use these words together to tie all these different ideas and meaning into a short 2 lines displays his well thought out lyricism and deep passion for his craft.

line: Way more money than I had back in the day
vault_lines: Way more money than I had back in the day
meaning:
Juice WRLD grew up in Calumet Park, Illinois, a small working class suburb just outside Chicago. He was raised primarily by his mother, who was strict and religious, and money was never abundant growing up. He’s mentioned in interviews that his mom worked hard to keep things stable but they were far from wealthy.

By 2018, at just 18 years old, he had signed one of the most talked about deals in rap, a reported $3 million deal with Interscope Records and Grade A Productions. Shortly after, Forbes estimated he had earned around $15 million by 2019, making him one of the highest earning young artists in the game at the time.

He reflected on the come up in a 2019 interview with Elevator saying “I went from having nothing to having everything real fast.” That kind of rapid financial shift is something he referenced constantly throughout his music, not always with celebration but sometimes with a sense of disbelief or even unease about how quickly everything changed.

line: Hop in a foreign and wreck the bitch, I feel so reckless
vault_lines: Hop in a foreign and wreck the bitch, I feel so reckless
meaning:
Juice WRLD grew up in Calumet Park, a working class suburb on the south side of Chicago. Coming from modest means, foreign cars (Lamborghinis, Ferraris, McLarens) represented the peak of the success he had chased. Once he blew up off “All Girls Are the Same” and signed his $3 million deal with Interscope/Grade A in 2018, he went on to spend heavily on luxury cars and designer goods almost immediately.

The recklessness he’s describing here isn’t just about driving though. It ties into a broader self-destructive streak that ran through his personality and his music. People close to him described Juice as someone who lived extremely fast and had little regard for consequences, whether that was with drugs, relationships, or just the way he carried himself in general.

There’s also something to be said about the “wreck the bitch” phrasing. It reflects a detachment from the material things he worked so hard to obtain, like he got the bag but doesn’t even care enough to preserve what came with it. That tension between achieving success and feeling empty or reckless inside is a theme he revisited constantly, most notably on tracks like “Robbery” and “Rich and Blind.”

line: Uh, I can’t take withdrawals, I’ma relapse again
vault_lines: Uh, I can't take withdrawals, I'ma relapse again
meaning:
Juice WRLD was one of the most candid artists about his drug addiction, specifically his dependence on lean (codeine syrup mixed with soda) and Percocet. In a 2019 XXL interview he admitted “it’s the hardest thing to stop,” and that he had tried to quit multiple times but kept falling back into it.

Withdrawal from opioids and codeine causes brutal physical symptoms including nausea, sweating, anxiety, and muscle pain that can last days or even weeks. For someone as deeply dependent as Juice was, relapsing wasn’t really a choice as much as it was the body demanding relief.

His manager and close friends had noted that Juice was using large amounts of lean daily by the time of his death. The night he died at Chicago’s Midway Airport in December 2019, federal agents had discovered 70 pounds of marijuana on his private jet. It was reported that Juice swallowed multiple Percocet pills in an attempt to hide them from agents before suffering a fatal seizure shortly after, a known risk of opioid overconsumption.

Cheetahs are the fastest land animals. They can reach speeds of up to 75 miles per hour (120 kilometers per hour) in short bursts over distances up to 1,500 feet (460 meters). Their long, muscular legs, flexible spines, and specialized respiratory and cardiovascular systems enable them to achieve this remarkable speed.

Molasses, on the other hand, is a thick, viscous syrup. It is produced during the refining of sugar cane or sugar beets. Because of its high viscosity, molasses flows slowly, making it a common metaphor for slowness or inertia:

I used to be a fast runner, but now I’m slow as molasses.



Cheetos Puffs, by contrast, are a popular snack known for their airy texture and cheesy taste. In this context, the mention of “puff” could be a play on words, referring to both taking a puff of a cigarette or marijuana and enjoying a Cheetos Puff snack.

While the link between “puff” and “Cheetah” through “Cheetos Puffs” is plausible, it’s important to acknowledge that it could be considered a bit of a stretch. The term “puff” is more commonly associated with smoking or leisure activities than with snack foods like Cheetos Puffs. However, given the creative nature of the lyrics and the potential for puns, it’s not entirely implausible that Juice WRLD intended this connection.

The line “Tryna sell my soul” suggests that he feels pressured to compromise his values or integrity in exchange for success or recognition. The notion of “selling your soul” is often used metaphorically to describe making compromises or sacrifices for personal gain.

Malcolm X rejected the pressure to conform and compromise his beliefs and instead chose to stand firm on his principles.

By comparing himself to Malcolm X, Juice WRLD implies that he refused to give in to the pressure to sell out or compromise his values for fame or fortune. The “X next to my name” symbolizes his commitment to stay true to himself and resist outside influences that seek to exploit or manipulate him.

meaning:
In a practice known as “drug lacing,” “laced blunts” are blunts mixed with other substances, such as LSD and PCP, or even more dangerous drugs like cocaine, heroin, and fentanyl. Although various substances can be used, intentionally lacing cannabis is uncommon, though, as always, it is not unheard of.

Juice WRLD was born in Chicago, Illinois, United States. The United States and Canada report some of the highest levels of drug adulteration and synthetic opioid-related harm, particularly involving illicitly manufactured fentanyl. Fentanyl and other synthetic opioids have been found mixed into substances such as counterfeit pills, cocaine, methamphetamine, and heroin, potentially to increase potency or reduce production costs, while consumers may sometimes be unaware that the substance is laced.

Tremors after cannabis use typically stem from high-THC overstimulation or an anxiety response rather than a laced product, though drug adulterants can trigger severe medical emergencies. Mild to moderate shivering or hand tremors can occur as a temporary reaction to THC, particularly after consuming a large amount. These standard “weed shakes” are generally harmless and fade within 15 to 30 minutes as the effects gradually wear off.

However, if a blunt actually is laced, shaking can occur because a foreign chemical affects the central nervous system. Stimulants like methamphetamine or cocaine can increase adrenaline and stimulate the nervous system, potentially causing muscle twitching, a dangerously rapid heart rate, and jaw chattering.

It’s also interesting to note that, thankfully, Juice never suffered any documented cases of drug-lacing-related medical emergencies. However, in many of his songs, he speaks about the physical side effects of taking potent drugs or large doses, such as in 2024’s “Party By Myself”:

“Chasing the dragon” is drug slang for inhaling heroin or another opioid more intensely to feel the first rush a person received the first time they used the drug.

meaning:
As Juice already explained, he meant money when he said “confetti” this is because, as you probably already know, most currency notes are printed in various shades of the same color to make it easy for people to distinguish between different denominations. However, some countries have chosen to use different colors for their currency notes to make them even more visually distinctive and easier to recognize.

For example, the Australian dollar has a unique color for each denomination, with the $5 note being purple, the $10 note blue, the $20 note red, the $50 note yellow, and the $100 note green. Similarly, the Canadian dollar also uses different colors for its notes, with each denomination having a distinct color. This practice of using different colors for currency notes helps people quickly identify the value of the note they are using or receiving, which is especially useful for those who may have difficulty distinguishing between similar colors.

So, to test it, I sat down with experienced Astrophysicist Donald Goldsmith. Don has received many awards for his work, and has written books alongside Neil DeGrasse Tyson so, if anyone knows what they’re talking about, it’s him.

“With that [Yung Bans’ lyric] in mind, what would you make of the flat earth theory?” I asked.

To which he responded: “First of all, there is no merit to it, because we have several millennia, but especially the space age, disproving it.”

“And, secondly, it obviously springs from human desires to believe in secret knowledge that’s being concealed from us, and to believe in something that makes a moment of sense, and you don’t have to give it up just because there’s a mountain of evidence against it.

Columbus was famous for watching ships disappear over the horizon – they slowly ‘sank’. To him this was proof, and it is proof, that they were sinking on a spherical Earth.”

Yung Bans’ claim that the Earth isn’t round is therefore false. Science can easily prove the spherical nature of our planet, and disprove the flat-earth theory.

line: Bitches love to tell tall tales, waggin’ I know that I’m a dog, but still Blood hounds feel pain like a human feels
vault_lines: Bitches love to tell tall tales, waggin'
I know that I'm a dog, but still
Blood hounds feel pain like a human feels
meaning:
Juice WRLD’s lyrics in this line involve clever wordplay and metaphors. Let’s break it down:


“Bitches love to tell tall tales, waggin',” – This line is a play on words. “Tell tall tales” is a common idiom that means to tell exaggerated or untrue stories. However, the word “tails” in this context is a homophone for “tales,” and it’s a clever pun, as he’s comparing people who gossip or spread rumors (“tell tall tales”) to dogs wagging their tails. Dogs wag their tails when they’re excited or happy, and in this context, he’s suggesting that some people enjoy gossiping or spreading exaggerated stories, and they get a certain satisfaction or excitement from doing so.
“I know that I’m a dog, but still,” – Here, Juice WRLD acknowledges that he’s aware of his own flaws or misbehaviors, and he’s using the metaphor of being a “dog” to represent someone who might not always act perfectly or who has a reputation for certain behaviors.
“Bloodhounds feel pain like a human feels.” – This line emphasizes the emotional aspect of his self-awareness. He’s saying that, despite his own shortcomings or flaws (comparing himself to a “dog”), he recognizes that even those who might be seen as tough or resilient (like bloodhounds, known for their tracking abilities) can still experience emotional pain just like humans. This is a reminder that everyone, even those who seem strong or unfeeling, can be affected by emotional pain.

line: This a touchy subject like hoes lying ’bout they body count
vault_lines: This a touchy subject like hoes lying 'bout they body count
meaning:
Juice WRLD’s line, “This a touchy subject like hoes lying ‘bout they body count,” uses a metaphor to describe a sensitive or delicate topic. In this line, he’s comparing the subject he’s discussing to the act of people, specifically women in this context, lying about the number of sexual partners they’ve had, which is commonly referred to as their “body count.”

The reason this is a touchy subject is because discussions about one’s sexual history or the accuracy of such claims can be personal and potentially controversial. Some people may feel uncomfortable or even judged when discussing or revealing their sexual experiences. By drawing this parallel, Juice WRLD is emphasizing that the topic he’s addressing in his lyrics is as sensitive and potentially contentious as the issue of dishonesty surrounding one’s sexual history.

line: Bitch, I’m not from NASA, but this drama got me spacin’
vault_lines: Bitch, I'm not from NASA, but this drama got me spacin'
meaning:
Juice WRLD’s line, “Bitch, I’m not from NASA, but this drama got me spacin',” can be interpreted as a clever play on words and a metaphorical expression. In this line, he’s using “NASA” as a reference to outer space, and he’s not literally saying he’s from NASA. Instead, he’s expressing how the drama and problems in his life have made him feel like he’s in outer space, distant from reality or normalcy.

The word “spacin'” is a colloquial term for feeling spaced out or mentally detached, which is often associated with being preoccupied or overwhelmed by issues. So, in essence, Juice WRLD is conveying that the stress and complications in his life have him feeling mentally distant like he’s lost in space. It’s a way of expressing the emotional and psychological toll of the drama he’s experiencing.

line: Funny how I went broke to rich in one year
vault_lines: Funny how I went broke to rich in one year

Juice signed a $3M record deal with Grade A Productions back in March 2018 after his record label’s co-founder, G-Money, discovered and played Juice’s breakout hits “Lucid Dreams” and “All Girls Are the Same” for his brother and fellow co-founder, Lil Bibby.

In an interview with XXL, Bibby recalled hearing the song for the first time and immediately recognizing Juice’s potential:

My brother is my partner with everything. He plays a big part. He found Juice [and] he brought him to me. He played me the song “All Girls Are the Same” and I was like, “Alright, that’s a good song.” Then he sent over some YouTube links, and I heard “Lucid Dreams.” When I heard “Lucid Dreams,” I’m like, “Oh, now this is probably the best song I’ve heard in over 10 years.” That’s when I really knew. line: I just fucked a bitch off a Perky and half a Xan’

meaning:
“Perky” is short for Percocet which is a prescription drug. Percocet comes in pill form and contains oxycodone hydrochloride and acetaminophen.

Percocet is a pain medicine but is often abused and misused. The high people get when misusing it occurs because of the oxycodone in it. When opioids attach to receptors in your brain and central nervous system, they block pain signals significantly but also trigger the release of dopamine, a chemical naturally associated with pleasure and satisfaction.

Some of the symptoms somebody might feel while high on Percocet include the following:  

-Euphoria: A sense of intense happiness or well-being.

-Relaxation: A calming effect that can lead to a feeling of tranquility.

-Drowsiness: Increased sleepiness or an inability to stay awake.

-Altered perception: Changes in how one perceives time and surroundings.

Percocet can also have dangerous side effects, usually occurring when somebody overdoses . Some of these dangerous effects include very small pupils, falling asleep or loss of consciousness, slow or shallow breathing, choking or gurgling sounds, vomiting,
pale or cold skin, faint heartbeat, along with purple lips and fingernails. In severe cases, the person may have a seizure or stop breathing which both can result in death.

Klonopin is a brand name for the drug clonazepam, which belongs to a class of medications called benzodiazepines. It is commonly used to treat anxiety, panic disorder, and seizures.

Klonopin works by increasing the activity of a neurotransmitter in the brain called GABA, which helps to calm the nerves and reduce feelings of anxiety or seizures. It is usually taken orally in tablet form, and the dosage and duration of treatment depend on the individual’s medical condition and response to the medication.

Like other benzodiazepines, Klonopin can cause drowsiness, dizziness, and impaired coordination, especially when first starting the medication. It can also be habit-forming and may cause withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly.
